The test image shows a soybean plant close-up at the stem/petiole junction. Key observations:
- **Dark brown/reddish-brown stem discoloration** — prominent necrotic browning of the stem
- Leaves appear mostly green with only minor spots
- The browning is concentrated on the stem, not the leaves
- Plant is pubescent (normal for soybean)

This stem necrosis pattern points to: Phytophthora, Brown_Stem_Rot, Rhizoctonia, Anthracnose, or Sudden_death_syndrome. Let me compare reference images.
Let me check a few more candidates to confirm.
Let me view two more references to finalize.

**Analysis Summary:**

- **Fusarium**: Root/crown rot with black roots and bleached stems — doesn't match
- **White_Mold**: White cottony mycelium on stems — clearly different

**Final Assessment:**

The test image shows a close-up of a soybean stem at the petiole/node junction with prominent **dark reddish-brown external stem discoloration** while the leaves remain green. This is the classic presentation of **Phytophthora** stem canker:
- External brown lesion wrapping around the stem at/near node
- Leaves still green (early-to-mid stage infection)
- No white mycelium (ruling out White Mold)
- No gray sclerotia (ruling out Charcoal Rot)
- Not hypocotyl-level (less consistent with Rhizoctonia seedling blight)

The Phytophthora reference collage (bottom-right panel) shows nearly identical brown stem node coloration — most visually consistent match among all classes reviewed.
